David / team — preliminary notes from infra: HarborLytics traffic was routed to the v2.q profile at 07:22 PST (can confirm in routing logs). We've observed two correlated signals: a sharp increase in attention-kernel compile misses on the int8 path for sequence lengths >1024, and elevated CPU overhead on the pre-/postprocessing host causing request queuing. Together those pushed p95 and increased request timeouts which manifest as 5xx.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Rollback HarborLytics to v1.fp16 (safe path, identical model binary) — fastest (~8-12 min to roll traffic and warm caches).
2) Disable int8 fused kernels for sequences >768 (complex, risk of partial regressions).

Recommendation: perform the rollback to v1.fp16 now, open an internal postmortem to root-cause the kernel mismatch, and schedule a controlled re-test of v2.q with a staged traffic ramp (canary + p95 guardrails).

I'll standby on the bridge. If agreed, I'll trigger the rollback with ops and confirm once KV caches are warmed.

—Rishi
